items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls or sessions; it sees only its current context. With nothing saved and re-loaded, Monday's chat does not exist for it. Options a and c show the misconception that the model automatically remembers earlier conversations (M3).

The contexts sent are 1,000, then 3,000, then 5,000, then 7,000 tokens, and 1,000 + 3,000 + 5,000 + 7,000 = 16,000. Answering 7,000 counts only the final context and misses that the transcript is re-sent whole on every call.

Retrieval searches the manual and adds only the best-matching chunks, keeping the context small and relevant. Sending everything (b) costs tokens each call and can hurt recall; the model's training does not hold this machine's manual (c); a fixed sample (d) will not contain the needed page.

items.answer: A student's training or certification status; the program loads it from storage (a database or notes file) at session start, or a tool reads it, and puts it into the new context.
accepted: Training status, loaded from a database into the context at the start of the session
Student preferences or past bookings, stored outside the model and read back into the context in the next session
items.rationale: Full credit needs both a suitable item (small, personal, needed later, not available elsewhere) and the load step: saved text is put back into the new context. Naming an item without saying how it returns is partial. Saying the model remembers or learns it is wrong (M3).

items.answer: Every token is billed on every call, so it costs more; and a crowded context can make the model worse at using the relevant information.
accepted: It costs more because you pay per token on each call
Too much text can reduce the model's accuracy in recalling what matters (context rot)
It raises cost and can lower quality
items.rationale: Either reason is fully correct: cost per token on every call, or degraded recall as the context grows. Saying only that it is slower or that the model gets tired is incomplete. Saying a bigger window removes any need to manage context is wrong (M7).
